summary.text: Anthony Constantino is the founder and CEO of Sticker Mule, a printing and technology company based in Amsterdam, New York, and the Republican nominee for the open 21st District seat. A first-time candidate, he won the June 2026 primary over Assemblyman Robert Smullen with President Trump's endorsement. He describes his campaign as self-funded and centered on immigration enforcement, healthcare costs and government spending.

paragraphs.text: Constantino founded Sticker Mule in Amsterdam in 2010, and WAMC reports it is now an international company employing more than 1,000 people. He describes himself as its founder and CEO.

In October 2024, he built a large "Vote for Trump" sign atop one of the company's Amsterdam factories overlooking I-90, which drew national attention. He also emailed Sticker Mule customers urging support for Trump, and says the email cost the company revenue.

According to his Ballotpedia survey, Constantino turned professional as a boxer for his 40th birthday and compiled a 2-1 record with two knockouts. He says he is fluent in Spanish and lists illegal immigration among the policy areas he is most passionate about.

Constantino is seeking a seat that opened when Rep. Elise Stefanik announced in December that she would not seek another term. President Trump endorsed him in April 2026, and WAMC reported he was the only Republican in the primary with that endorsement; the station had described him as a political outsider facing the establishment-backed Assemblyman Robert Smullen.

He defeated Smullen in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary, 59.2% to 40.3%. Constantino will also appear on the independent Taxpayer Rights line in November. His Democratic opponent is Blake Gendebien.
